subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Modern prose or drama — one set text

questions.q: How long is the AQA GCSE English Literature Paper 2 exam?
questions.explain: Paper 2 (Modern Texts and Poetry) is a written exam lasting 2 hours 15 minutes.

questions.q: What percentage of the overall GCSE grade does Paper 2 carry?
questions.explain: Paper 2 is worth 96 marks and 60% of the total GCSE, with Paper 1 accounting for the remaining 40%.

questions.q: What are the three sections of Paper 2, in order?
options: Modern texts, Anthology poetry, Unseen poetry
questions.explain: Section A is Modern texts, Section B is Anthology poetry comparison, and Section C is Unseen poetry.

questions.q: In Section A, what type of text does a student write about?
options: One modern prose or drama set text
questions.explain: Section A requires an essay on the one modern prose or drama text the student has studied, such as An Inspector Calls or Lord of the Flies.

questions.q: Which assessment objective is assessed in Section A of Paper 2 but not in Sections B or C?
questions.explain: AO4 (SPaG) is assessed only in the Section A modern texts response, worth 4 of that section's 34 marks.

questions.q: Is Paper 2 an open-book or closed-book examination?
options: Closed book — no copies of the texts permitted
Students may bring the anthology only
questions.explain: AQA GCSE English Literature is a closed-book exam, so students may not take copies of set texts or the anthology into the exam.

questions.q: How is the Section A modern texts question presented to students?
options: A choice of two essay questions on the studied text
questions.explain: For each set text students are offered a choice of two whole-text essay questions and answer one.

questions.q: A response to a modern text is being marked for AO3. What is the examiner mainly rewarding?
options: Understanding of the relationship between the text and its context
questions.explain: AO3 rewards showing understanding of the ideas, perspectives and contextual factors shaping a text and how it was received.

questions.q: A student writes about how Priestley uses the Inspector to promote ideas of social responsibility in 1912-set Britain. Which assessment objective does this contextual comment chiefly address?
questions.explain: Linking the play's message to its social and historical context is an AO3 skill.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the current AQA poetry anthology clusters?
questions.explain: The three clusters are Love and relationships, Power and conflict, and Worlds and lives; students study one.

questions.q: How many anthology clusters does a student study for Section B?
questions.explain: Students study a single cluster of 15 poems and answer on it in Section B.

questions.q: How is the Section B anthology question structured?
options: Analyse one named poem in isolation
Compare a named, printed poem with another chosen poem from the same cluster
Compare a poem with an unseen poem
Write about any two poems from any cluster
questions.explain: One poem from the cluster is named and printed on the paper, and students compare it with another poem they select from the same cluster.
'Ozymandias', a sonnet on the transience of power, was written by Percy Bysshe Shelley and sits in the Power and conflict cluster.

questions.q: In a Section B comparison, a student closely analyses metaphor, structure and rhyme to explain their effects. Which assessment objective is central to this?
questions.explain: Analysing language, form and structure and their effects using subject terminology is the AO2 skill.

questions.q: A student wishes to compare the printed poem 'My Last Duchess' with 'Ozymandias' in Section B. Why is this a valid pairing?
options: Both belong to the Power and conflict cluster
Both are from the Love and relationships cluster
questions.explain: Section B comparisons must be drawn from within the same studied cluster, and both poems are in Power and conflict.

questions.q: How many unseen poems appear in Section C of Paper 2?
questions.explain: Section C presents two previously unseen poems: one is analysed in full and both are compared.

questions.q: What does the first (24-mark) unseen poetry question ask students to do?
options: Analyse one unseen poem and how the poet presents a theme
Relate the poem to its historical context
questions.explain: The 24-mark question asks for a close analysis of a single unseen poem and the ideas and methods within it.

questions.q: What is the focus of the second, shorter (8-mark) unseen poetry question?
options: The context in which the poems were written
Comparing the methods the two poets use
Evaluating which poem is better written
questions.explain: The 8-mark question asks students to compare the poetic methods used in the two unseen poems.

questions.q: Reading an unseen poem, a student identifies enjambment and a regular iambic rhythm and explains how they shape meaning. This demonstrates which assessment objective?
questions.explain: Naming poetic techniques and explaining their effects on meaning is an AO2 skill, which dominates the unseen poetry section (AO3 context is not assessed there).

specSource: AQA GCSE English Literature (8702) specification; Paper 2: Modern Texts and Poetry
